segments.narration: The soil above this grave is thick with mercury. Lintong, near Xi'an, under a hill seventy-six metres tall.
Farmers digging a well in 1974 hit its outer edge. Thousands of terracotta soldiers, standing in battle formation.
Those were the guards. The tomb itself has never been opened. A historian writing a century later said it held a hundred rivers of mercury, flowing mechanically, under a ceiling of stars.
For centuries that read as legend. Then surveys measured the soil: mercury far above the regional background, clustered where China's real rivers would sit on a map.
So archaeologists stopped. Terracotta paint flaked away within minutes of exposure in 1974, and nobody can promise better today. The rivers stay sealed until technology catches up.

verdicts.claim: The mausoleum of Qin Shi Huang stands in Lintong District, Xi'an, Shaanxi, under a burial mound about 76 metres tall, and soil surveys there found anomalously high mercury.
verdicts.note: 77% of the claim's wording appears in the reference article, including 1 number(s)

verdicts.claim: Farmers digging a well found terracotta warrior fragments in March 1974, and excavation revealed about 7,000 terracotta figures in battle formation.
verdicts.note: Wikipedia: farmers found fragments in March 1974, formal excavation began May 1974, three major pits hold about 7,000 statues of warriors and horses arranged in formation.

verdicts.claim: Sima Qian, writing roughly a century after the burial, described mercury made to simulate the hundred rivers, the Yangtze, the Yellow River and the sea, set to flow mechanically, beneath a representation of the heavens.
verdicts.note: 74% of the claim's wording appears in the reference article

verdicts.claim: Soil surveys measured mercury far above the regional background over the tomb mound, with the highest readings clustered in a pattern resembling the geography of China's rivers.
verdicts.note: Wikipedia gives an average around 205 ppb over 53 points with one at 1,440 ppb; ExplorersWeb reports the Institute of Geophysical and Geochemical Exploration finding about 250 ppb over the vault against roughly 30 ppb regionally, peaking near 1,500 ppb, with high readings to the northeast and south matching the Yellow River and Yangtze. The two summaries differ slightly on the exact figures, so the narration states the comparison and not a number.

verdicts.claim: The central tomb chamber has never been excavated on preservation grounds, including the rapid deterioration of pigment on terracotta figures once exposed in 1974.
verdicts.note: Wikipedia gives preservation concerns as the reason the main chamber is unopened and cites terracotta paint deteriorating rapidly on excavation; ExplorersWeb additionally notes the mercury hazard.
